## Summary

1. Every runtime reject in every run is the same evaluator error: an ordered comparison whose operand is a bare constant (the model wrote `greater than equal( height, 900 mm)` with `height` as a bare entity instead of an attribute); the frozen v1 translator renders bare all-alpha operands as constants, and the evaluator refuses to order a constant against a number. Opus never writes this; the other three models do.
2. These are not policy-P3 violations: P3 (totality) requires every well-formed IR to translate, and it does; the programs parse and pass the safety check, and the reject happens in the evaluator. The v1.1 addendum's "translator bug by P3" clause covers safety/stratification failures of v1.1's own output, which never occur here.
3. They are, however, the M2c defect (F3 in the v1.1 ledger: bare entity operands as dead constants), so the corrected translator is the right upper bound: the "v1.1 evaluable" column counts rejected IRs that evaluate on every case under v1.1, and "v1.1 exact" how many of those then pass their suite.
4. The paper's best-of-four upper bound (Table 2) is Opus only, and Opus has no rejects in the plain run; for the other models the rejects are absorbed only where the paper reports v1.1 numbers (Haiku plain). The override runs use the v2 grammar, to which v1.1 does not apply.
5. Under the frozen primary a rejected suite scores 0 of its cases, so the rejects depress the non-Opus LRML-IR case-level numbers and cannot change the exact-suite ordering (a rejected suite is already a failed suite).
